svg.title: State Summary launcher, classification, summarization and report workflow
svg.desc: The launcher starts Python, which reads the state-news archive, filters the last 24 hours, classifies headlines, summarizes accepted stories, writes reports and exports data for the web viewer.
svg.text: STATE SUMMARY: from launcher to policy briefings
Follow stateSummary.ps1 through its Python analysis, generated reports and the State Summary web viewer.

g.text: Start the PowerShell launcher
Append transcript to C:\Scripts\stateSummary.txt.
Set the working directory to the WCS project.
Run Python in the Pipenv environment
Loop over the launcher script list (currently one):
pipenv run python ./scripts/stateSummary.py
Upstream input
stateNews.py runs separately.
RSS feeds are listed in
static/media_outlets.csv.
Their text and metadata
populate the states archive.
Load, deduplicate & filter the archive
Read masterdata/states.csv.
Deduplicate exact titles first; keep the first row.
Then keep articles published in the last 24 hours.
Map each outlet to a state
Read the name -> state lookup from
static/media_outlets.csv and replace the name field.
Classify headlines into six policy topics
facebook/bart-large-mnli on CUDA GPU 0.
Process headline batches of 16 with multi-label scores.
Select only the highest-scoring topic per article.
Topic thresholds
State Budget: .70
K-12 Education: .70
Public Health: .70
Public Opinion Polls: .70
Protests / civil unrest: .95
Immigration / enforcement:
Skip this article
classified_issue = None.
Remove it before sending
articles to the summarizer.
Pass accepted articles to summarization
Carry the assigned state, topic and headline score.
Keep the article text, source title, outlet and URL.
No second topic is assigned if the top topic fails.

svg.text: Accepted stories, within the same Python run

g.text: Prepare each accepted article's text
Use up to four concurrent worker threads.
Strip HTML tags and collapse whitespace.
Build a prompt with the state and assigned issue.
Empty cleaned text?
Return no summary for that article.
The active path uses the text field; it has
no explicit description fallback.
Generate an issue-focused summary
POST to localhost:11434/api/generate.
Actual default model: mistral-nemo; stream=False.
Prompt requests <= 5 sentences about the issue,
favoring government, policy and political impacts.
No usable model response?
An API error returns an empty string.
Empty responses or a literal SKIP are omitted.
Each summary request has a 600-second timeout.
The script continues with other articles.
Collect summaries by state and issue
Gather worker results as they finish.
Store summary, title, outlet, URL and headline score.
Article order follows completion, rather than date.
Clean the summary text
Remove bullet characters and asterisks; trim spaces.
Keep each summary with its original story metadata.
Write the reports and data exports
development/state_issue_summary.json
development/issue_weekly_report.docx
development/state_weekly_report.docx
uploads/state_summary.csv
CSV: state, topic, outlet, headline, summary, URL.
Outputs use the same file paths on each run.
State Summary web viewer
Flask serves templates/state_summary.html.
D3 loads the CSV and displays linked headlines
with summaries, grouped State -> Topic or
Topic -> State. Jump links include story counts.
Fetch the timestamp for the last-updated label.
Log the result & finish the run
Append timestamp + row count to static/stateSummary.json.
Request Ollama to unload mistral-nemo (keep_alive=0).
Return to PowerShell and stop the transcript.

svg.text: Issue-first Word report: topic -> states. State-first Word report: state -> topics, with a page break per state.
Both include linked headlines and summaries. The web viewer offers both grouping modes for the same exported stories.

g.text: Actual data window
The analysis uses the last 24 hours by published date.
It does not use firstEyes for eligibility.
The 'weekly' filenames do not change this window.
One topic per story
Six scores are calculated; only the top topic is considered.
A below-threshold top score means the story is skipped.
There is no review queue or alternate-topic fallback.
Reading this chart
Solid arrows: processing or an acceptance decision.
Dashed arrows: upstream/viewer inputs or skip branches.
The viewer reads files; it is not launched by PowerShell.

svg.text: Source: scripts/stateSummary.ps1, stateSummary.py, stateNews.py, getFunc.py, app.py and templates/state_summary.html.
The launcher currently calls only stateSummary.py. State-news collection and web deployment are separate operations.
